newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-NEWCASTLE OVERWHELM MIDDLESBROUGH TO GO TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-NEWCASTLE OVERWHELM MIDDLESBROUGH TO GO TOP.

text.p: Newcastle skipper Peter Beardsley scored twice as his team beat Middlesbrough 3-1 to go top of the English premier league on Sunday -- then said they were more determined than ever to win the title.

The evergreen Beardsley, 36 in January but playing with the pace and enthusiasm of a man 10 years younger, marked his 700th league and cup appearance with a goal in each half as Newcastle won a blood-and-thunder 99th derby against their old north-east rivals.
Robert Lee scored his first goal for 18 matches since last April to put Newcastle 3-0 up. Danish international Mikkel Beck scored a late consolation for Middlesbrough.

Newcastle, chasing their first championship title since 1927, were pipped by Manchester United after leading the table for most of last season, and Beardsley said on Sunday that disappointment was driving the team now.

"That was a terrible disappointment for everyone here," he said. "But it has given us a mental toughness and determination that maybe we did not have before. It has made us harder to beat, I am sure."

Manager Kevin Keegan echoed his skipper's words when he said: "To be honest, going back on top of the table doesn't thrill me. We were top for a long while last season and look what happened. I am looking for performances and winning matches like today's, in a very tough local derby, was very satisfying."

Passion, red-blooded challenges and intriguing little rivalries were all over the field in a match which featured internationals from 11 countries and players who had cost Keegan and Middlesbrough manager Bryan Robson 65 million pounds ($106.6 million) to buy.
And that total does not include Newcastle's world record, 15.0 million pounds ($24.61 million) signing Alan Shearer, who missed the match following groin surgery.

With the victory, Newcastle leapfrogged two points clear of Arsenal, who drew 2-2 at Wimbledon on Saturday, and four points clear of third-placed Liverpool, who crashed to a 3-0 defeat at bottom-of-the-table Blackburn earlier on Sunday.
Significantly Newcastle are now eight points clear of sixth-placed Manchester United, who lost 2-1 at home to Chelsea on Saturday.

Middlesbrough battled Newcastle for every ball, but the home side took control four minutes before half-time when Beardsley, who missed a penalty against Ferencvaros in the UEFA Cup on Tuesday, gave Boro keeper Gary Walsh no chance with his spot-kick.
"He couldn't have missed that," said Keegan afterwards. "His son Drew was one of the ball boys and can you imagine what would have happened if he'd have seen his dad miss a penalty?
"Great players write their own scripts. You felt he would get a hat-trick and he nearly did."
The referee judged Neil Cox brought down David Ginola, and although the Middlesbrough players hotly disputed that decision Robson said afterwards he thought the referee was right.

Beardsley put Newcastle 2-0 after 70 minutes with a powerful low drive after Les Ferdinand found him in space. Five minutes later Lee made it 3-0 with a shot that took a wicked deflection off a Middlesbrough defender.
Beck had a great opportunity to score when he found himself in front of an open goal in the 81st minute but lashed the ball against the bar, before scoring his side's consolation goal.

"We never reached the heights we did when we beat United 5-0 or Ferenccaros 4-0 on Tuesday, but those three points will do for me," added Keegan, who has now seen his side undefeated in eight north-east derbies over the last four years against both Sunderland and Middlesbrough.
Middlesbrough, who started the season very well while Newcastle made a slow start, have now picked up just two points from their last six matches and have slipped to 15th.

Robson, a Newcastle fan as a schoolboy, said: "I congratulate Newcastle, they played well. There is not all that much wrong with my team but obviously we must start getting a few victories under our belts."
"I don't think we deserved to get beaten by three goals. We were containing Newcastle quite well in the first half, then we had five mad minutes leading up to the penalty."
"I didn't think Newcastle cut us up. It was mainly our own mistakes at the back."

But while Newcastle look for more glory, their 24-year-old midfielder Lee Clark, who has played 200 matches for the club, asked for a transfer on Sunday after failing to win a regular place in the team.
